audit_findings.title: Finite swap income may be capitalized while the related derivative liability is omitted
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 swap benefit $36.1 million, equal to 20.9% of the $172.5 million anchor; June 2026 derivative liability $315.8 million, or $3.34 per share; net valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Swap receipts reduce net interest expense retained in equity-level OE, while any associated settlement claim is absent from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Included in Interest expense, net within the Consolidated Statements of Income are benefits of $ 36.1 million, $ 38.4 million and $ 38.8 million for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively, related to net interest payments received from counterparties.
audit_findings.explanation: The recurring inclusion of swap receipts in reported interest expense is demonstrated, but the record does not establish whether the OE interest-income purge removed them or whether the derivative liability is economically offset by the hedged foreign investment. If the $36.1 million benefit was normalized as perpetual OE despite finite swap terms, the scale relative to the anchor is material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year to gross debt interest, cash interest, and swap receipts; obtain June 2026 settlement terms and fair values; then rerun the valuation after removing only temporary net benefits and recognizing any non-offset settlement claim.

audit_findings.title: The ten-year anchor may combine materially different business perimeters
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquisitions, divestitures, financing changes, and stranded corporate costs can alter historical OE, its fitted trend, and the resulting $172.5 million anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Through a series of acquisitions, divestitures, operational improvements and cultural shifts, the Company has transformed to become an innovator of materials solutions.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates substantial transformation, but it does not quantify current-perimeter OE for the ten historical years. The direction could be higher or lower, and the record cannot establish whether a reconstructed trend would materially differ from the selected anchor.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct 2016-2025 OE on the June 2026 operating perimeter, including acquired and disposed operations, transaction financing, and stranded costs, and rerun the log-trend anchor and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Accrued environmental remediation is an unfunded claim ahead of equity
audit_findings.magnitude: June 2026 environmental accrual $132.3 million, including $123.1 million for Calvert City; $1.40 per share and 4.6% of $2,849 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Future remediation cash payments either reduce projected OE when paid or require a bridge deduction if the anchor does not carry that cash burden.
audit_findings.evidence: Total environmental accruals of $ 141.2 million and $ 146.0 million are reflected within Accrued expenses and other current liabilities and Other non-current liabilities in our Consolidated Balance Sheets as of December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The claim and its omission from the bridge are demonstrated, although whether a separate deduction would double count remediation already represented in historical OE remains unresolved. Deducting the full recorded accrual would reduce base value from $30.12 to about $28.72 per share, which does not change the conclusion at a $43.40 market price. Additional costs are probable but unquantified and are not covered by this scale conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Map historical environmental charges and cash payments into OE, project the filed payment schedule, deduct the $132.3 million only to the extent not already captured, and separately stress-test the unestimated additional Calvert City costs.

audit_findings.title: All cash may not be distributable to common shareholders at carrying value
audit_findings.magnitude: $425.6 million added to the bridge; approximately $332.0 million, or 78%, held outside the United States; actual distributability haircut unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Repatriation taxes, withholding taxes, legal restrictions, and required operating liquidity reduce the cash available for addition to common-equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: It is not practical to estimate the additional income taxes and applicable withholding taxes that would be payable upon the remittance of such undistributed earnings.
audit_findings.explanation: The foreign location of most cash and indefinite-reinvestment policy are demonstrated, but foreign cash is not necessarily trapped and the filing says the remittance tax cannot practicably be estimated. The possible haircut is large enough to affect reported value, but the record cannot establish its amount or materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain cash by legal entity and jurisdiction, minimum operating-cash requirements, remittance restrictions, tax attributes, and estimated withholding and repatriation costs; rerun the bridge using only distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: A large nonrecurring insurance recovery may contaminate the trend anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $34.7 million pre-tax 2024 recovery; actual after-tax effect on the fitted $172.5 million anchor unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An episodic insurance gain can inflate 2024 OE and therefore the ten-year log-trend anchor used in every scenario.
audit_findings.evidence: We recognized gains from insurance recoveries of $ 2.0 million , $ 34.7 million and $ 1.7 million in 2025 , 2024 and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The $34.7 million nonrecurring recovery is demonstrated, but its inclusion in the supplied 2024 OE and its exact influence on the fitted trend are not established. Because it is concentrated in a recent trend year, it may affect value, but materiality cannot be determined without the OE reconciliation and trend rerun.
audit_findings.action: Trace the 2024 gain and related cash receipt through the OE calculation, apply the correct tax treatment, remove any included nonrecurring amount, and rerun the ten-year trend and scenarios while retaining recurring remediation economics.

audit_findings.title: The equity bridge omits an unreserved tax dispute
audit_findings.magnitude: $36.8 million known claim comprising $23.8 million tax, $8.2 million estimated interest, and $4.8 million penalty, plus unquantified further interest; $0.39 per share and 1.3% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A probability-weighted adverse tax settlement would be deducted in the equity bridge unless already reflected in normalized OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the Company has not recorded any income tax provision related to this matter; therefore an unfavorable ruling or settlement in U.S. Tax Court would adversely impact our effective tax rate and result in a cash tax payment.
audit_findings.explanation: The dispute is demonstrated, but an obligation is not: Avient contests it and has recorded no provision. Even deducting the entire currently quantified $36.8 million would lower base value only from $30.12 to about $29.73 per share and would not change the conclusion at $43.40.
audit_findings.action: Update the Tax Court status, accrued interest, counsel's probability assessment, and any settlement range; probability-weight the exposure and rerun the bridge if the quantified claim expands materially.
